question_stem:
A uniform plank AB of length 5.0 m and weight 200 N is placed across a stream, as shown in
Fig. 3.1.
A man of weight 880 N stands a distance x from end A. The ground exerts a vertical force F_{A} on
the plank at end A and a vertical force F_{B} on the plank at end B.
As the man moves along the plank, the plank is always in equilibrium.
question_stem_latex:
A uniform plank AB of length 5.0 m and weight 200 N is placed across a stream, as shown in
Fig. 3.1.
A man of weight 880 N stands a distance x from end A. The ground exerts a vertical force $F_{\mathrm{A}}$ on
the plank at end A and a vertical force $F_{\mathrm{B}}$ on the plank at end B.
As the man moves along the plank, the plank is always in equilibrium.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.question_text:
Explain why the sum of the forces F_{A}and F_{B}is constant no matter where the man stands
on the plank.
parts.question_text_latex:
Explain why the sum of the forces $F_{\mathrm{A}}$and $F_{\mathrm{B}}$is constant no matter where the man stands
on the plank.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.question_text:
The man stands a distance x = 0.50 m from end A. Use the principle of moments to
calculate the magnitude of F_{B}.
parts.question_text_latex:
The man stands a distance x = 0.50 m from end A. Use the principle of moments to
calculate the magnitude of $F_{\mathrm{B}}$.

parts.label: (b)
parts.question_text:
The variation with distance x of force F_{A} is shown in Fig. 3.2.
On the axes of Fig. 3.2, sketch a graph to show the variation with x of force F_{B}.
parts.question_text_latex:
The variation with distance x of force $F_{\mathrm{A}}$ is shown in Fig. 3.2.
On the axes of Fig. 3.2, sketch a graph to show the variation with x of force $F_{\mathrm{B}}$.
